newsitem.title: FRANCE: French television seen politically biased - poll.
newsitem.headline: French television seen politically biased - poll.

text.p: Mainstream French television channels are seen by the public as politically biased, according to a poll published on Tuesday.

The poll, carried out on May 10, in the middle of a French election campaign, by polling insitute IFOP for monthly television magazine Television-Le Mensuel, found 60 percent of those questioned thought television channels were not really independent of government influence.

Pay television channel Canal Plus, whose current affairs coverage and talk shows are broadcast uncoded, came top for lack of political bias, with 27 percent saying it was the most independent channel.
Publicly-owned arts channel Arte came second with 19 percent, followed by the four general terrestrial channels, with TF1 scoring 16 percent and M6 13 percent.
Public channels France 2 and France 3 came bottom with nine percent and six percent respectively designating them as the most unbiased channel. The remaining 10 percent had no opinion.
"There is no right of appeal. Practically two French people out of three believe the channels are not independent of government," Television-Le Mensuel said.
Despite their distrust of television channels' impartiality, 52 percent of those surveyed said they trusted television to keep them informed about France's political goings-on.
Those who did not trust television reporting to keep them informed came to 47 percent, with only one percent declining to express an opinion.
"A paradox -- French people do not think the channels are politically independant, but a small majority trusts them to keep them informed about French political life," the magazine said.
Mainstream television has come under attack in France of late.

Advertising industry specialist Carat said over a million viewers switched off in the first few months of this year compared to a year earlier, but television audience measurment body Mediametrie denied this was the case.
A two-stage parliamentary election is being held on May 25 and June 1.
